question: A monochromatic electromagnetic wave propagates in free space along the $+x$ direction. At a certain point and time, the electric field is measured to be $\vec{E}(x,t) = E_0 \cos(\omega t - kx) \hat{j}$. A student makes the following claim: "Since the wave is travelling along $x$ and $\vec{E}$ is along $y$, the magnetic field can also be along $y$ as long as its magnitude satisfies $B_0 = \frac{E_0}{c}$." Evaluate the claim using the properties of electromagnetic waves in free space and identify the correct expression for $\vec{B}(x,t)$ and the direction of energy flow.

options.A: $\vec{B}(x,t) = \frac{E_0}{c} \cos(\omega t - kx) \hat{k}$ and energy flows along $+x$
options.B: $\vec{B}(x,t) = \frac{E_0}{c} \cos(\omega t - kx) \hat{j}$ and energy flows along $+x$
options.C: $\vec{B}(x,t) = \frac{E_0}{c} \cos(\omega t - kx) \hat{i}$ and energy flows along $+z$
options.D: $\vec{B}(x,t) = \frac{E_0}{c} \sin(\omega t - kx) \hat{k}$ and energy flows along $-x$
